title: How AUSL athlete Maya Johnson uses lab testing to manage lupus while competing at the highest level
summary: Maya Johnson shares her lupus journey and how regular lab testing helps her manage symptoms, monitor lupus flares, and compete at a high level.
body_markdown:
For years, Maya Johnson knew something wasn't right.


When she was in seventh grade, she began feeling unusually tired. As time went on, she developed additional symptoms, including joint pain, rashes, and ongoing fatigue.


"It was about three and a half years of unexplained symptoms," Johnson recalls.


Finally, during her sophomore year of high school, Maya met with a rheumatologist and underwent blood work and testing. At age 15, she received a diagnosis: lupus.


For many people, receiving a diagnosis of a chronic illness can feel overwhelming. For Maya, it brought relief.


"I didn't know what I was experiencing, and it didn't really seem like anyone had the answers," she says. "The lupus diagnosis was a big sigh of relief because it pointed us toward the next steps."


**A path forward**


Lupus is a chronic autoimmune disease that can affect many parts of the body and cause symptoms such as fatigue, joint pain, and inflammation.


As an elite athlete, Maya learned that living with lupus requires careful planning and flexibility. She often experiences increased soreness and slower recovery after training. To help protect her health and performance, she adjusts workouts, monitors fatigue levels, and works closely with her medical team.


"If I'm more fatigued or having a lupus flare, I might not pitch at all or lower my pitch count," she says.


**The role of testing in managing lupus**


An important part of Maya's care plan is regular lab testing.


She completes blood work every six to eight weeks to help monitor inflammation and track how her body is responding to treatment. When symptoms increase, additional testing can help identify whether a lupus flare may be occurring.


By combining lab results with how she feels physically, Maya can better understand when to rest and when she can safely return to higher levels of activity.


**Breaking barriers for other athletes**


Today, Maya plays professional softball in the Athletes Unlimited Softball League (AUSL) and has achieved many of the goals she dreamed about as a child. She was a two-time First Team All-American, helped her college team win back-to-back conference championships, and became the first mid-major athlete drafted into the AUSL.


By speaking publicly about her experience, Maya hopes to help others recognize symptoms sooner and seek medical attention when something feels wrong. She also wants young athletes with chronic illnesses to know that their diagnoses don’t have to define their futures.


"I want youth athletes who are experiencing chronic health issues to know that there is a path to playing at the highest level," she says.


**Monitoring health through testing**


[Labcorp is working](https://www.labcorp.com/patients/ausl) with the AUSL to advance women’s health and support athlete well-being. As part of this collaboration, we're sharing stories from players about the role testing has played in their lives. We hope Maya's story highlights how lab testing can help people better understand chronic conditions and monitor changes in their health.
